The API producer catalog (services/api/src/queue/derived-assets-queue.ts:38-44) and the POST run zod enum (services/api/src/routes/media-intelligence.routes.ts:1462-1468) carry only the first 5; video_keyframe/screen_reconstruction are written only by the UC-4 orchestrator. packages/shared/src/evidence-acquisition.ts:537-543 also declares screen_crop, which has NO producer anywhere.

reviewed.note: FAILED/UNSUPPORTED writes COALESCE the artifact columns so a previously stored object stays counted/destroyable; bytes route serves only COMPLETED (media-intelligence.routes.ts:1384).

previousStorage is DELETED after a successful regeneration (no history kept) unless an effective hold is active, in which case the old object is kept with no row pointer. Superseded objects are lost from the list if the run throws or returns descriptor_too_large before line 536. Destruction still reaches such orphans via the derived-assets/<evidenceId>/ prefix sweep (packages/shared-runtime/src/evidence-destruction/executor.ts:142-149,754-763). See UC-DER-006.
Derived rows, OCR/transcript/extracted text, semantic chunks, search docs deleted in the tombstone tx; objects enumerated from rows AND the derived-assets/<evidenceId>/ prefix.
Runs every orchestrator tick, bounded 200 tombstones, objects-before-rows, hold-guarded. Also incidentally sweeps any derived row written after destruction (see UC-DER-013).

reviewed.topic: Derived bytes authorization (view-only role, byte-release gate)

The tab is shown only when acquisition.category === DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE (Android frame, Android continuous, iOS); hidden for UC-1 web captures and uploads. Nothing enqueues it automatically on capture/finalize. The API does NOT restrict to screen evidence: any image/video part of any team evidence is processed (handler.ts:115-132). Generation is NOT gated by OCR policy; OCR is gated at run time on workspace_ai_policies.ai_enabled && ocr_allowed, default false (no row => false). With OCR off the run still extracts keyframes and completes with zero blocks, coverage PARTIAL, UI says 'OCR is disabled'. reviewed.evidence: packages/shared/src/evidence-acquisition.ts:35-91 (7 acquisition modes: PROOVRA_WEB_UPLOAD, SECURE_INTAKE_LINK, PROOVRA_MOBILE_APP, DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION, DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_ANDROID, DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_ANDROID_CONTINUOUS, DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS)
reviewed.note: There is no conversation/chat-export/messaging-API capture channel. 'Conversation' exists only as the name of a DERIVED OCR-based screen reconstruction transformation (screen-conversation-reconstruction/v1). WhatsApp is a retired intake DELIVERY channel, not a capture channel.

Single ffmpeg pass fps=1000/1500ms, ≤240 frames/part, output kf-%04d.webp. offsetMs = (i-1)*intervalMs is NOMINAL (derived from the output index), not the decoded frame PTS and not relative to the container start_time; VFR screen recordings get approximated offsets. Offsets are part-relative; no absolute UTC mapping. Offset persisted to source_offset_ms (screen-intelligence.service.ts:286) but NOT projected by listDerivedAssetsForEvidence (derived-assets.service.ts:253-258) nor the package manifests.

reviewed.topic: Keyframe producer: tool version / parameters / output digest
reviewed.note: Output sha256 per keyframe recorded (derived_sha256, content-addressed key). ffmpeg binary version never recorded (engineVersion hard-coded 'uc4-screen-intelligence-v1'), parameters (interval, max frames, scale 256, q75) not recorded, parameters_sha256 null. UC-DER-005.

reviewed.topic: Keyframes: duplicates, long video, corrupt media, unsupported codec
reviewed.note: Duplicates: fixed-interval sampling (the change-scored selectKeyframes in packages/shared/src/screen-keyframes.ts:66 is used only by the test-only runScreenIntelligence) so a static screen yields many identical keyframes, identical bytes share one content-addressed key. Long video: >240 frames (6 min) flags RECONSTRUCTION_BOUNDS_REACHED; the 60 s ffmpeg timeout fails the part -> POSSIBLE_GAP. Corrupt/unsupported codec: ffmpeg non-zero exit -> part skipped with the generic RECONSTRUCTION_POSSIBLE_GAP; the concrete reason (ffmpeg_exit..., non_video_mime, no_keyframes_produced) is discarded at screen-intelligence.service.ts:246-251 and never shown. A truncated-but-decodable source (range cap) yields no limitation (UC-DER-014).

Local, argv spawn, 30 s timeout, TSV parse into line regions with bbox + mean confidence; version from `tesseract --version` banner (cached); eng+ara packs installed. Failure per frame throws -> counted in stats.ocrFailedKeyframes, frame degraded. Engine unavailable -> run proceeds with OCR disabled (labelled as 'disabled by policy', UC-DER-008). Language and bbox are returned but dropped downstream (UC-DER-005). OCR runs on 256-px keyframes for video (UC-DER-003).

reviewed.topic: OCR text persistence / digest / failure visibility
reviewed.note: OCR_SCREEN + SCREEN_RECONSTRUCTION EvidenceExtractedText rows replaced per run (deleteMany then create), language null, confidence null, extractedAtUtc null, no text digest; failures swallowed silently (catch at 690) — a run can be COMPLETED while search text persistence failed with no signal.

reviewed.topic: Reconstruction core: ordering authority & message identity
reviewed.note: Ordering authority = evidence_parts.part_index then frameOrder (keyframe index) then OCR rowOrder (vertical position). Message identity: blockId = representative observation id 'obs-N' — positional, regenerated each run, not stable. No provider message id.

reviewed.topic: Reconstruction: actor attribution, visible timestamps, tz
reviewed.note: NO actor attribution is claimed: the only OCR provider emits kind 'TEXT' for every region; VISIBLE_LABEL / VISIBLE_TIMESTAMP / MEDIA / SYSTEM kinds exist in the type but nothing produces them. No on-screen timestamp parsing, no timezone handling. Copy correctly says a visible label is not a verified identity.
Not modelled: blocks are OCR text lines only. No attachment detection, no thread/reply structure, no edit/deletion markers.
Missing context flagged RECONSTRUCTION_POSSIBLE_GAP when no overlap is found. But the overlap test cannot succeed on real messaging screens, so duplicates are the norm. UC-DER-004.

reviewed.note: Descriptor keeps observations (machine-extracted) separate from blocks (reconstructed); projection carries DERIVED_RECONSTRUCTED / DERIVED_MACHINE_EXTRACTED markers; coverage never exceeds acquisition completeness (screen-intelligence.service.ts:419-436); UI/report carry standing 'not original acquisition' copy. Everything is stored as EvidencePartDerivedAsset, never as an EvidencePart.
Claim/lease/fence correct for the first run; reuse-by-idempotency-key makes every later run impossible. UC-DER-001.

Reads the persisted descriptor only (no mock), paginates 100, per-block View Source with keyframe thumbnails and Open Original. Shows the last COMPLETED descriptor even when the latest run FAILED, without saying it is from an earlier run (generatedAtUtc not rendered). DISMISSED state has no action button (dead end, UC-DER-001).

Counts/coverage/limitations/transformation versions only, never text — correct separation. Not tied to the descriptor it summarises (no digest, generatedAtUtc passed but not rendered): UC-DER-015. Returns null for NULL-team records.

Lineage-only manifests (no derived bytes): derived/derived-manifest.json, intelligence/derived_assets manifest, intelligence/screen_reconstruction_manifest.json. Silently truncated (UC-DER-007); descriptor digest TOCTOU (UC-DER-015).

reviewed.topic: Can a report/package include an old derivative as current
reviewed.note: Yes in two ways: (a) keyframe variants from an earlier run that the new run did not rewrite stay COMPLETED and are listed by loadDerivedArtifacts/listDerivedAssetsForEvidence; (b) a regeneration that returns descriptor_too_large (or throws after keyframes persisted) leaves the previous descriptor COMPLETED while its keyframe rows (same ids) now hold new bytes, so the descriptor's per-keyframe derivedSha256 no longer matches the served bytes. No staleness check compares source_sha256_at_generation to evidence_parts.sha256 anywhere (only projected: provenance-chain.ts:317,338; verification-package.ts:1363).

Provider/providerVersion/language/confidence recorded when the provider returns them; no source digest, no text digest; text silently truncated at MAX_TEXT_BYTES with no flag; each run CREATEs a new row (the 'upserted' doc comment at 135-136 is false) so stale rows accumulate. AI-policy/provider aspects belong to the AI area; not audited in depth here.
No production writer; still swept on destruction.
Row-level facts (not bytes); parser name stored on the part (technical_meta_parser). Not audited in depth (no byte release, no object).

Released only through evaluateArtifactDownload kind 'redaction' with the explicit redaction.derivative.download capability (ET-SEC-26 fixed). Destruction enumerates redactionDerivative objects (executor.ts:721-724). Redaction internals belong to the redaction area.

reviewed.topic: Reports / verification packages / downloadable originals as byte releases
reviewed.note: All go through the one gate (permission, personal-owner rule, policy, export eligibility incl. hold/trash). The derived-assets bytes route is the remaining byte-release path outside it (UC-DER-002).

Row-level advisory signals with engine_version; no source digest; swept on destruction? not in the executor's derived deletes (only via evidence FK-less table) — not verified in depth, outside DER scope.

Team-anchored, storage keys never projected (OK). Omits variant_key, transformation, parameters_sha256, source_offset_ms, so 240 keyframes/part are indistinguishable rows in the API, the Technical Appendix strip (UC-DER-011) and the intelligence package manifest.

findings.title: Derived Review 'Retry' and 'Regenerate' never run: the reused run row is COMPLETED/DISMISSED and the worker claim refuses it, while the API answers 202 queued
findings.userImpact: After the first run, Regenerate does nothing (status stays COMPLETED with the old reconstruction). After any failure, Retry moves the run to DISMISSED and the tab then shows 'Dismissed' with no button at all — UC-4 is permanently dead for that evidence. After 5 claims (attempt_count ceiling) the same key can never run again either.
findings.legalImpact: A reviewer who regenerates after an OCR/engine change believes the review reflects the new run; it is the old one.
findings.reproduction: 1) Generate Derived Review on a DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE record; run -> COMPLETED. 2) Click Regenerate: route 1560-1570 finds prior COMPLETED run; dismissRun (run-tracker 388-393) only matches PENDING/FAILED/PROCESSING so nothing changes; enqueueMediaIntelligenceAnalysis -> enqueueMediaIntelligenceRun reuse path (run-tracker 146-165) returns the SAME COMPLETED row (idempotency key `reconstruct_screen:<evidenceId>`, unique index media_intelligence_runs_team_idemp_uk), job is enqueued with that run id; worker markRunProcessing UPDATE predicate (239-247) requires PENDING/FAILED or expired PROCESSING -> 0 rows -> reason max_retries_exceeded (257) -> handler.ts:81-89 bumps DLQ and returns ok. 3) Make a run fail (e.g. descriptor_too_large or storage outage exhausting retries) then click Retry: dismissRun sets FAILED->DISMISSED, reuse returns the DISMISSED row, claim refuses, tab shows 'Dismissed' with no action (tab 90-119 has buttons only for NOT_REQUESTED/FAILED/COMPLETED||projection).
findings.observed: API 202 {queued:true}; nothing is regenerated; DISMISSED is terminal with no UI action; no test covers regenerate (grep of derived-review tests).
findings.expected: Regenerate/Retry creates a fresh run (new row or reset of the settled row to PENDING with attempt_count 0) and the worker processes it; a refused claim on an explicit user request is reported, not drained as success.
findings.rootCause: The idempotency key is per (kind, evidence) forever and the reuse path ignores status; the route's 'dismiss then re-enqueue' assumes a new row will be inserted, but the unique key and the status-blind reuse return the settled row, which the exclusive claim correctly refuses.
findings.remediation: In the generate route, for regenerate: atomically reset the settled run (COMPLETED/FAILED/DISMISSED -> PENDING, attempt_count 0, fence bump) or rotate the idempotency key (e.g. include a generation counter); make enqueueMediaIntelligenceRun reuse only non-terminal runs; surface a refused claim as FAILED with a reason instead of DLQ-silent success; add a Retry action for DISMISSED.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: generate->complete->regenerate produces a second COMPLETED run with a new descriptor generatedAtUtc; fail->retry runs again; attempt ceiling reached -> explicit user regenerate still runs.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB + Redis + worker with ffmpeg: POST generate, wait COMPLETED, POST generate {regenerate:true}, assert media_intelligence_runs row count/status and descriptor generatedAtUtc unchanged (demonstrates defect).

findings.title: Derived bytes (low-res proxy video, frames, keyframes, full OCR reconstruction JSON) are released on evidence.read alone, outside the byte-release authority: VIEWER, legal hold, trash, destruction review and workspace download policy are all bypassed
findings.userImpact: A VIEWER, who is refused original bytes even for in-app viewing (originalReleaseForViewer -> evidence.download_original), can fetch a 480p re-encode of the video, 256-px keyframes of every 1.5 s, and the screen_reconstruction JSON containing every OCR'd line of the recording. Trashed, held and destruction-bound records keep serving these bytes.
findings.legalImpact: Legal-hold 'no byte release' rule and export eligibility do not govern derivative bytes; content of a held/trashed record can leave through derivatives.
findings.securityImpact: Within-tenant privilege bypass of the download capability model (read access => content export via derivatives). No cross-tenant exposure (team-anchored).
findings.reproduction: As a VIEWER member of team T: GET /v1/evidence/<id>/derived-assets?teamId=T (authorizeOrFail evidence.read, 1277) -> bytesUrl per COMPLETED row; GET that bytesUrl (1333-1443): authorizeOrFail evidence.read (1346), evidence team check without deletedAt/lifecycle (1353-1359), status COMPLETED (1384), streams the object. The screen_reconstruction row's bytes are application/json with all observations[].text. Repeat with the record trashed or under an active legal hold: still 200.
findings.observed: No call to evaluateArtifactDownload; ArtifactKind has no derivative kind (gate.service.ts:67); VIEWER lacks evidence.download_original (permissions.ts:533-549) yet receives derived content.
findings.expected: Derived byte release decided by the one gate: a derivative-appropriate permission, personal-owner rule, export eligibility (hold/trash/destruction review) and policy — or an explicit, documented decision that thumbnail-class derivatives are in-app view material, with proxies/keyframes/reconstruction JSON gated.
findings.rootCause: The Phase 31.14 bytes proxy predates the 2026-09-29 single byte-release authority and was never folded into it (the redaction derivative was, ET-SEC-26).
findings.remediation: Add a 'derived' ArtifactKind to evaluateArtifactDownload (with a recordDenial:false view mode for thumbnails) and call it from the bytes route; at minimum refuse deletedAt/TRASHED/PENDING_DESTRUCTION and held records for proxy/keyframe/reconstruction kinds and require download_original for low_res_proxy/video_keyframe/screen_reconstruction.
findings.requiredTests: Route tests: VIEWER denied proxy/keyframe/reconstruction bytes; held record denied; trashed record denied; OWNER allowed; custody EXPORT_BLOCKED_BY_POLICY on denial.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB: seed team, VIEWER member, evidence with a COMPLETED screen_reconstruction derived row + object in a local S3 stub; place ACTIVE legal hold; GET bytes as VIEWER -> expect 403, observe 200.

findings.title: Local OCR for every video-based screen capture runs on keyframes downscaled to at most 256 px wide
findings.userImpact: For Android continuous and iOS screen recordings the reconstruction is built from OCR of thumbnail-resolution frames (a 1080-px-wide phone screen is scaled ~4.2x down, 40-px text becomes ~9 px), so text is largely missed or garbled; the Derived Review looks empty or noisy while reporting OCR 'enabled'.
findings.legalImpact: Machine-extracted text presented as review material is systematically degraded; omissions are not flagged as a limitation.
findings.reproduction: produceVideoKeyframes builds `-vf fps=1000/1500,scale='min(256,iw)':-2` (ffmpeg-derived-assets.ts:159); the orchestrator pushes kf.bytes as the frame to OCR (screen-intelligence.service.ts:306-314) and calls deps.ocr.extractFromBytes(frame.bytes) (355). UC-2 still images are OCR'd at full resolution (316-329), so only video sources are affected.
findings.observed: OCR input width <= 256 px for all video parts.
findings.expected: OCR on full-resolution frames (a separate OCR frame extraction or a keyframe rendition sized for OCR), with the review thumbnail kept small.
findings.rootCause: The keyframe rendition reuses the video_frame thumbnail sizing, and the same bytes feed OCR.
findings.remediation: Extract OCR frames at native resolution (to temp only, or a separate 'ocr_frame' variant) and keep 256-px keyframes for display; record the OCR input resolution in the descriptor.
findings.requiredTests: Worker test with a real screen-recording fixture: OCR recall of known on-screen strings above a floor; descriptor records OCR input dimensions.
findings.runtimeProbe: Worker image with ffmpeg+tesseract: run produceVideoKeyframes on a chat screen recording, OCR the kf bytes vs the native frame; compare recognised word counts.

findings.title: Reconstruction de-duplication cannot merge real messaging screens: every message is repeated once per keyframe and HIGH_OVERLAP is practically unreachable
findings.userImpact: The 'reconstructed reading order' lists the same message many times (one block per 1.5 s keyframe it was visible in), in sequence, as separate blocks; a reviewer can read repeats as repeated messages. Coverage is always PARTIAL with POSSIBLE_GAP even for a clean continuous scroll.
findings.legalImpact: Duplicated blocks in an ordered 'conversation' reconstruction can be mistaken for repeated sends; duplication is not labelled as such (only 'overlap PARTIAL_OVERLAP').
findings.reproduction: (a) Fixed chrome: frame A rows [Header, m1, m2, m3, Composer], frame B rows [Header, m2, m3, m4, Composer]. scrollOverlap (121-134) needs the last k rows of A to equal the first k rows of B; A ends with 'Composer', B starts with 'Header' -> k=0 -> possibleGap, no union: m2/m3 become two blocks each. (b) Static screen: identical consecutive keyframes give k = full frame; geometryCorroborates (142-155) requires a fingerprint on every row, but the Tesseract provider never sets fingerprint (82-89) and the runtime uses fixed-interval sampling (ffmpeg-derived-assets.ts:159) rather than the change-scored selectKeyframes (screen-keyframes.ts:66, used only by the test-only runScreenIntelligence) -> not merged, flagged gap. (c) rowsMatch is exact text equality (106-112), so OCR jitter between frames breaks any overlap.
findings.observed: Blocks = union components that almost never union; confidence HIGH_OVERLAP requires >=2 frames in one component (249).
findings.expected: Overlap detection that tolerates fixed header/footer regions and OCR noise (e.g. content-region cropping, fuzzy/normalised match, bbox-aware), change-based keyframe selection or frame-hash de-dup, and visible labelling of residual possible duplicates.
findings.rootCause: The deterministic core assumes the whole frame scrolls and OCR is exact; the runtime supplies neither fingerprints nor change-scored frames that the core's safety rules rely on.
findings.remediation: Exclude persistent top/bottom rows (rows identical across all frames of a part) before overlap; match on normalised text with bbox tolerance; emit a per-frame pixel hash as fingerprint; skip keyframes identical to the previous; mark blocks with observedInFrames==1 adjacent to an identical-text block as POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE.
findings.requiredTests: Pure tests with header/composer rows and one-line scroll; static-screen sequence; OCR-jitter sequence; assert no duplicate blocks and correct coverage.
findings.runtimeProbe: Pure unit (no runtime needed): feed reconstructScreenConversation two frames with fixed header/composer rows and a one-message scroll; observe duplicated blocks and RECONSTRUCTION_POSSIBLE_GAP.

findings.title: Derivative/OCR provenance fields are dropped: no OCR language, no region geometry, no real tool versions, no generation parameters, no text digest
findings.userImpact: A reviewer or validator cannot tell which language model OCR used (eng+ara by env), where on the frame a line was read, which ffmpeg/sharp build produced a derivative, or what sampling parameters were used; regeneration cannot be proven equivalent.
findings.legalImpact: Reproducibility of machine-derived material (tool + version + parameters) is not recorded, weakening any explanation of how derived text was produced.
findings.reproduction: Tesseract adapter returns {regions (with bbox, confidence), language: lang} (tesseract-ocr-provider.ts:152); the orchestrator keeps only res.regions (screen-intelligence.service.ts:356) and builds observation records without bbox (368-393; type descriptor.ts:106-120); descriptor ocrProvider = {name, version, local} (444) — no language; OCR_SCREEN row language: null, confidence/extractedAtUtc unset (649-661). Keyframe/descriptor rows use engineVersion 'uc4-screen-intelligence-v1' (145) and sharp/ffmpeg rows 'sharp-v0-phase31-v1'/'ffmpeg-v0-phase31-20' (processor.ts:66,70) — constants, not binary versions; ffmpeg-capability probes `-version` but discards the output. No producer ever sets parameters_sha256 (only read at provenance-chain.ts:319, verification-package.ts:1368). No digest of extracted text anywhere.
findings.observed: Fields exist in schema/types but are null or constant.
findings.expected: Descriptor and rows record OCR language, per-observation bbox, tesseract version (already known), ffmpeg/sharp versions from the probe, a canonical parameters JSON + parameters_sha256 (interval, max frames, scale, quality, psm), and a sha256 of persisted extracted text.
findings.rootCause: Lineage columns were added at UC-0 but producers were not updated to fill them; the observation record type omitted geometry.
findings.remediation: Thread language + bbox into ScreenObservationRecord; capture binary versions in capability probes; compute parametersSha256 in each producer; add text sha256 to EvidenceExtractedText (or the descriptor).
findings.requiredTests: Unit: descriptor contains language, bbox, parametersSha256; derived rows have non-null parameters_sha256 and a probed engine version.
findings.migrationImpact: additive (optional text digest column); otherwise none
findings.runtimeProbe: Run one UC-4 job against a disposable DB; SELECT parameters_sha256, engine_version FROM evidence_part_derived_assets; parse descriptor JSON for language/bbox.

findings.title: Regeneration silently overwrites derivative lineage in place and deletes the prior object; stale keyframe variants survive; no custody/audit record of derived generation
findings.userImpact: A reconstruction a reviewer relied on (and that an earlier report summarised) is replaced with no trace; descriptorVersion is always 1 and the row id is reused, so there is no way to see what changed or when beyond updatedAt.
findings.legalImpact: Machine-derived review material can change after it was used in review or summarised in a report, with no custody event and no retained prior version.
findings.reproduction: recordDerivedAsset ON CONFLICT (team, part, kind, variant) DO UPDATE (derived-assets.service.ts:173-196) returns previousStorage; callers delete it (processor.ts:702; orchestrator 536-543). The descriptor variant is the constant 'recon-v1' (500) and descriptorVersion defaults to 1 (440; no caller passes it). Extracted text rows are deleteMany'd and recreated (636-641). If a regenerated part's ffmpeg pass fails (246-251 'continue') or yields fewer frames, its earlier kf-NNNN rows stay COMPLETED and are still listed by listDerivedAssetsForEvidence / loadDerivedArtifacts though the new descriptor does not reference them. No appendCustodyEvent/audit write in the generate route (1531-1591), processor or handler.
findings.observed: History replaced; stale variants retained as current; no custody trail.
findings.expected: Versioned derivatives (new variant or retained prior object + row with superseded status), removal/marking of variants not produced by the current run, and a custody/audit event for derived generation and regeneration.
findings.rootCause: UC-0's 'never orphan a pointer' rule was implemented as replace-and-delete rather than versioning; the orchestrator never reconciles the previous run's variant set.
findings.remediation: Bump descriptorVersion per run and key the descriptor variant by it (recon-v<N>), mark superseded rows SUPERSEDED instead of overwriting, delete or supersede keyframe variants absent from the new run, and append a DERIVED_GENERATED custody event with the descriptor digest.
findings.requiredTests: Regenerate with a changed bound -> old descriptor retained as superseded, new version current, orphan keyframes marked, custody event present.
findings.migrationImpact: additive (status value / optional custody event type)
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB: run UC-4 with maxKeyframesPerPart=10 then 5 (bounds override); count COMPLETED video_keyframe rows (10) vs descriptor.keyframes (5).

findings.title: Package derived manifests are silently truncated (500 / 200 rows) and report the truncated number as the count
findings.userImpact: A continuous screen recording easily exceeds the caps (up to 240 keyframes per part); the package's derived lineage lists a subset with no truncation marker, and review-artifact-boundaries.json states a derivedCount equal to the truncated list.
findings.legalImpact: Verification package describes an incomplete derived-material inventory as complete.
findings.reproduction: loadDerivedArtifacts findMany take: 500 ordered createdAt asc (provenance-chain.ts:308-323) feeds derived/derived-manifest.json (verification-package.ts:3546-3558) and derivedCount (3289-3291). buildDerivedAssetsManifest writes count: Math.min(assets.length, 200) and slices items (verification-package-intelligence.ts:323-324). Additionally the listDerivedAssetsForEvidence projection (derived-assets.service.ts:253-258) omits variant_key and source_offset_ms, so keyframe entries in the intelligence manifest are indistinguishable.
findings.observed: No 'truncated' flag or total count in either manifest.
findings.expected: Full lineage (paginate/stream) or an explicit totalCount + truncated:true with the bound; keyframe entries carry variantKey and sourceOffsetMs.
findings.rootCause: Bounds sized for Phase-31 thumbnails (one per part) were not revisited when UC-4 added many-per-part variants.
findings.remediation: Emit totalCount and truncated in both manifests (or remove the caps with streaming), project variantKey/sourceOffsetMs/transformation, and compute derivedCount from a COUNT query.
findings.requiredTests: Package test with 600 derived rows: manifest totalCount=600 and truncated flag (or 600 items).
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB: insert 600 COMPLETED video_keyframe rows for one evidence, build package, inspect derived/derived-manifest.json items length (500) and boundaries derivedCount.

findings.title: OCR engine unavailable is reported as 'OCR disabled by policy'
findings.userImpact: When the workspace allows OCR but the worker has no tesseract, the tab says 'OCR is disabled for this workspace' and the report says 'OCR: disabled by policy', sending admins to the wrong setting.
findings.legalImpact: Report states a policy decision that was not made.
findings.reproduction: ocrAllowed=true, detectTesseractCapability fails -> ocrProvider null -> enabled: Boolean(ocrProvider)=false (handler 164-166,201) with version 'unavailable' (199); UI/report branch only on ocrEnabled.
findings.observed: Single boolean conflates policy-off and engine-missing.
findings.expected: Distinct state (OCR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE) surfaced in descriptor limitations, UI and report.
findings.rootCause: Descriptor has no OCR-disabled reason field.
findings.remediation: Add ocrDisabledReason ('policy'|'runtime_unavailable') to the descriptor and render it.
findings.requiredTests: Handler test with policy on + missing binary -> reason runtime_unavailable; report copy.

findings.title: Derived bytes are cached 'immutable' for 24 h under a URL keyed by the reused row id, so regenerated derivatives display stale bytes
findings.userImpact: After regeneration the browser keeps showing the old thumbnail/keyframe for up to a day.
findings.reproduction: bytesUrl is /derived-assets/<rowId>/bytes (1303); the row id is stable across regenerations (upsert 173); response sets 'private, max-age=86400, immutable' (1434) on the claim that the bytes are content-addressed — the storage key is, the URL is not.
findings.expected: Include derivedSha256 in the URL (cache-bust) or drop 'immutable' and rely on ETag revalidation.
findings.rootCause: Content-addressing applied to the storage key only.
findings.remediation: Append &v=<derivedSha256 prefix> to bytesUrl or use no-cache + ETag.
findings.requiredTests: Route contract: bytesUrl changes when derivedSha256 changes.

findings.title: Personal (NULL-team) screen captures show the Derived Review tab but can never generate derived assets or UC-4
findings.userImpact: A personal user's Android/iOS screen capture shows a 'Derived Review' tab whose Generate button is disabled (or 404s) with no explanation.
findings.reproduction: CaptureSession.teamId is nullable (schema.prisma:1888) so personal screen captures exist; evidence_part_derived_assets.team_id and media_intelligence_runs.team_id are NOT NULL (14287, 14544); the generate route requires evidence.teamId === body.teamId (1553); the tab sources teamId from workspace.reviewWorkflow?.teamId and disables actions when null (39, 94); OCR policy returns false for null team (screen-ocr-policy.ts:29); report bridge returns null (derived-review-bridge.ts:20). The tab is still shown because visibility depends only on acquisition category (page.tsx:937-946).
findings.observed: Feature visible but unreachable for Personal records.
findings.expected: Either support Personal owners (owner-scoped derived rows) or hide the tab / explain why.
findings.rootCause: Derived-asset and run tables are team-keyed; the personal-owner model was never extended to derivatives.
findings.remediation: Resolve the owner's personal team for NULL-team records (as the byte gate does for holds) or hide the tab with an explanation.
findings.requiredTests: Web: tab hidden/explained for NULL-team record; API: personal owner can generate if supported.

findings.title: Technical Appendix 'Derived previews' renders every UC-4 keyframe and the reconstruction JSON as generic 'Derived preview' images
findings.userImpact: Up to 240 keyframes per part appear as unlabelled 'Derived preview' tiles with no offset, and the screen_reconstruction JSON tile shows 'Derived preview unavailable' (an of application/json).
findings.reproduction: DerivedAssetsStrip renders all COMPLETED rows (507, 545-553) as (612); humanAssetKind has no video_keyframe/screen_reconstruction case (739-753) -> 'Derived preview'.
findings.observed: Misleading broken tile and unlabelled flood.
findings.expected: Filter UC-4 kinds out of the strip (they belong to Derived Review) or label them with offset and never a JSON asset.
findings.rootCause: UC-4 reused the derived-asset table without updating the Phase-31 strip.
findings.remediation: Exclude video_keyframe/screen_reconstruction from DerivedAssetsStrip; link to the Derived Review tab.
findings.requiredTests: Component test with keyframe + reconstruction rows.

findings.title: Derived Review keyframe omits crossOrigin='use-credentials', which the sibling panel documents as required for the authenticated cross-origin bytes route
findings.userImpact: Per the codebase's own note, the keyframe thumbnails under 'View source' may 401 in production (runtime-dependent on cookie/SameSite).
findings.reproduction: MediaIntelligencePanel.tsx:630-632 comments that without crossOrigin='use-credentials' the browser omits the session cookie and the image 401s; EvidenceDerivedReviewTab.tsx:288-294 renders the same bytes URLs without it.
findings.observed: Inconsistent attribute on the same authenticated endpoint.
findings.expected: Same credentialed image loading as the panel.
findings.rootCause: UC-4 tab written without the NEW-028 fix.
findings.remediation: Add crossOrigin='use-credentials' and an onError state.
findings.requiredTests: Playwright: View source thumbnails load against a cross-origin API.
findings.runtimeProbe: Browser against prod-like split origins: open View source and inspect the keyframe request status.

findings.title: Derived producers never re-check record lifecycle before writing; runs on trashed records proceed and a run straddling destruction writes derived bytes/text onto the tombstone
findings.userImpact: Trashed records keep getting new derivatives (via the stranded-run reconciler, which does not filter lifecycle); after destruction, a late write re-creates derived rows/objects and OCR_SCREEN text until the next orchestrator sweep.
findings.legalImpact: A short window where destroyed evidence's derived content exists after the destruction certificate.
findings.reproduction: Source queries join evidence without deleted_at/lifecycle predicates (handler.ts:97-105; processor.ts:211-219); stranded media-intelligence runs are re-enqueued with no lifecycle filter (reconciler 224-248, unlike the derived-asset scan at 579-590); evidence_part_derived_assets has no FK (migration 20260620100000 CREATE TABLE at 1499) so an insert after destruction succeeds; EvidenceExtractedText insert succeeds on the retained tombstone row.
findings.observed: No lifecycle guard at write time.
findings.expected: Producers refuse (and drain) when the record is trashed / PENDING_DESTRUCTION / DESTROYED, checked immediately before persisting.
findings.rootCause: Lifecycle eligibility was added to the derived-asset reconciler only.
findings.remediation: Add an eligibility re-read before each persist in the orchestrator and processor; filter the stranded-run reconciler by lifecycle.
findings.requiredTests: Trash between enqueue and processing -> no derived rows written.

findings.title: Derivatives are generated from a range-capped, version-unpinned, unhashed read of the source while recording the whole part's digest as the generation source
findings.userImpact: A 'Low-res proxy' is at most the first 30 s and the first 50 MB of the source; video_frame reads 50 MB; thumbnails 4 MB; UC-4 64 MB. Nothing marks the derivative as partial.
findings.legalImpact: source_sha256_at_generation asserts a relationship to the full original that was not verified (bytes never hashed; S3 VersionId not used although evidence_parts.storage_version_id exists).
findings.reproduction: getObjectRange bytes=0-(budget-1) with no VersionId (storage.ts:249-265); no comparison with evidence_parts.size_bytes; produceLowResProxy passes '-t 30' (ffmpeg-derived-assets.ts:308-309); sourceSha256AtGeneration = part.sha256 (processor.ts:366,545; orchestrator 280,496). UC-3 segments are capped at 64 MB (packages/shared/src/screen-continuous-manifest.ts:145) so UC-4 on UC-3 is unaffected; uploads and generic videos are affected.
findings.observed: Partial derivatives recorded as derived from the whole part.
findings.expected: Read the signed version (storageVersionId), record bytes-read/whole-source flag and source range/duration in parameters, or add a limitation when truncated.
findings.rootCause: Bounded reads were added for resource safety without provenance for the bound.
findings.remediation: Pass VersionId; add truncated/sourceRange to parameters JSON; UC-4: add RECONSTRUCTION_SOURCE_TRUNCATED when bytes.length === maxBytes.
findings.requiredTests: Processor test with a source larger than the budget -> derivative carries truncated flag.

findings.title: Report and package cannot be bound to the exact reconstruction they describe (no digest/time in the report; package digest read from a separate query)
findings.userImpact: After a regeneration there is no way to know which descriptor a report's 'Machine-Derived Review Materials' counts came from.
findings.legalImpact: Weakens traceability of the report's derived-material statement.
findings.reproduction: Bridge passes generatedAtUtc (derived-review-bridge.ts:65) but the renderer never prints it and no digest is passed (derived-review.ts:65-93). The package bridge reads the descriptor bytes (119-148) but takes descriptorSha256 from derivedRows listed earlier (75-81,152-156) instead of hashing the bytes it read; a regeneration in between pairs one descriptor's digest with another's content.
findings.expected: Render descriptor sha256 + generatedAtUtc in the report; compute the package digest from the bytes read.
findings.rootCause: Summary-only design omitted the binding identifiers.
findings.remediation: Hash the read bytes in readScreenReconstructionDescriptor and return it; render it in the report section.
findings.requiredTests: Report snapshot contains descriptor digest; package digest equals sha256 of the descriptor bytes used.
